# agentplan Full Reference

agentplan is a CLI task-queue for AI agents to manage multi-session projects with tickets, dependency graphs, and progress logs.
It is designed for terminal-native automation loops where multiple agents share one persistent queue.

Version in this repository: `0.2.0`

## Installation

```bash
pip install agentplan
```

## Runtime and storage

- Backend: SQLite (single file)
- DB defaults:
  - `AGENTPLAN_DIR=~/.agentplan`
  - `AGENTPLAN_DB=~/.agentplan/agentplan.db`
- Important env vars:
  - `AGENTPLAN_DIR`: directory that stores default DB
  - `AGENTPLAN_DB`: explicit DB path (overrides default path)

## Command index

```text
agentplan init
agentplan version
agentplan create <title> [--ticket <text> ...] [--notes <text>]
agentplan ticket add <project> <title> [--depends <id_csv>] [--notes <text>]
agentplan ticket done <project> <ticket_id...>
agentplan ticket skip <project> <ticket_id...>
agentplan ticket start <project> <ticket_id>
agentplan ticket list <project> [--status pending|done|in-progress|skipped|all]
agentplan next [project]
agentplan status [project] [--format compact|full|json]
agentplan list [--status active|completed|paused|abandoned|all]
agentplan attach <project> <label> <location> [--ticket <id>]
agentplan log <project> <entry> [--ticket <id>]
agentplan close <project> [--abandon]
agentplan note <project> <text> [--ticket <id>]
agentplan depend <project> <ticket_id> --on <id_csv>
agentplan remove <project> [--ticket <id>]
```

## Command details

### `agentplan init`
Initializes database tables in configured DB path.

Example:
```bash
agentplan init
```

### `agentplan version`
Prints CLI version.

Example:
```bash
agentplan version
```

### `agentplan create <title> [--ticket ...] [--notes ...]`
Creates a project with slug derived from title.
- `title` (positional): project title
- `--ticket` (repeatable): seed tickets in order
- `--notes`: optional project note

Examples:
```bash
agentplan create "Build API"
agentplan create "Build API" --ticket "Schema" --ticket "Endpoints" --notes "MVP first"
```

### `agentplan ticket add <project> <title> [--depends ...] [--notes ...]`
Adds a ticket to project.
- `project`: slug or numeric project id
- `title`: ticket text
- `--depends`: CSV list of ticket numbers in same project
- `--notes`: optional ticket note

Behavior:
- Assigns next sequential `num` within project.
- Validates dependency ticket numbers.
- Rejects circular dependencies.
- Reopens `completed`/`abandoned` projects when adding new ticket.

Examples:
```bash
agentplan ticket add build-api "Write tests"
agentplan ticket add build-api "Load test" --depends 2,3 --notes "k6 baseline"
```

### `agentplan ticket done <project> <ticket_id...>`
Marks one or more ticket numbers as `done`.
- Auto-completes active project when all tickets are done/skipped.

Examples:
```bash
agentplan ticket done build-api 2
agentplan ticket done build-api 3 4 5
```

### `agentplan ticket skip <project> <ticket_id...>`
Marks one or more ticket numbers as `skipped`.

Example:
```bash
agentplan ticket skip build-api 9
```

### `agentplan ticket start <project> <ticket_id>`
Marks one ticket as `in-progress`.

Example:
```bash
agentplan ticket start build-api 4
```

### `agentplan ticket list <project> [--status ...]`
Lists tickets in project.
- `--status`: `pending|done|in-progress|skipped|all`
- Default behavior in parser: `all` when omitted

Examples:
```bash
agentplan ticket list build-api
agentplan ticket list build-api --status pending
```

### `agentplan next [project]`
Shows currently actionable tickets.
- If project provided: checks only that project.
- If omitted: scans active projects.
- Includes `in-progress` tickets plus pending tickets whose dependencies are satisfied.

Examples:
```bash
agentplan next
agentplan next build-api
```

### `agentplan status [project] [--format ...]`
Shows project status.
- `--format`: `full|compact|json`
- Default: `full`
- With no project: active projects

Examples:
```bash
agentplan status
agentplan status build-api --format compact
agentplan status build-api --format json
```

### `agentplan list [--status ...]`
Lists projects.
- `--status`: `active|completed|paused|abandoned|all`
- Default: `active`

Examples:
```bash
agentplan list
agentplan list --status all
```

### `agentplan attach <project> <label> <location> [--ticket ...]`
Adds attachment at project or ticket level.
- If `location` starts with `http://` or `https://`, stored as URL.
- Otherwise stored as path text.

Examples:
```bash
agentplan attach build-api "Spec" docs/spec.md
agentplan attach build-api "PR" https://github.com/org/repo/pull/10 --ticket 4
```

### `agentplan log <project> <entry> [--ticket ...]`
Writes log entry at project or ticket level.

Examples:
```bash
agentplan log build-api "Merged schema migration"
agentplan log build-api "Fixed flaky test" --ticket 7
```

### `agentplan close <project> [--abandon]`
Closes a project.
- Default status set to `completed`.
- `--abandon` sets status to `abandoned`.

Examples:
```bash
agentplan close build-api
agentplan close build-api --abandon
```

### `agentplan note <project> <text> [--ticket ...]`
Sets note text on project or one ticket.

Examples:
```bash
agentplan note build-api "Track breaking changes"
agentplan note build-api "Need canary rollout" --ticket 6
```

### `agentplan depend <project> <ticket_id> --on <id_csv>`
Adds dependencies to an existing ticket.
- `--on` required CSV of ticket numbers
- Merges with existing dependencies
- Rejects circular dependencies

Examples:
```bash
agentplan depend build-api 4 --on 1,2
agentplan depend build-api 5 --on 4
```

### `agentplan remove <project> [--ticket ...]`
Removes a ticket or whole project.
- With `--ticket`: deletes that ticket and removes dangling deps from other tickets.
- Without `--ticket`: deletes whole project and cascading rows.

Examples:
```bash
agentplan remove build-api --ticket 3
agentplan remove build-api
```

## Exit behavior summary

- Exit code `0`: successful command.
- Exit code `1`: generally used for empty result views (`list`/`next`/`ticket list` without items).
- Exit code `2`: argument/lookup/validation/runtime errors (not found, invalid ticket id, circular deps, etc.).

## Output formats

### `status --format full`
- Human-readable multiline board including ticket icons, blocked reason, attachments, recent logs, project notes.

### `status --format compact`
- Single concise line suitable for LLM prompt context.

### `status --format json`
- JSON object with project metadata and embedded tickets.

## Data model and schema

All tables are created by `init_db`.

### `projects`
- `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`
- `slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`
- `title TEXT NOT NULL`
- `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'`
- `notes TEXT`
- `created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT local timestamp`
- `updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT local timestamp`

### `tickets`
- `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`
- `project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
- `num INTEGER NOT NULL` (human-facing ticket number scoped to project)
- `title TEXT NOT NULL`
- `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'`
- `depends_on TEXT DEFAULT '[]'` (JSON array of ticket numbers)
- `notes TEXT`
- `created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT local timestamp`
- `completed_at TEXT`

Indexes:
- `UNIQUE INDEX idx_ticket_project_num ON tickets(project_id, num)`

### `attachments`
- `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`
- `project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
- `ticket_id INTEGER REFERENCES tickets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
- `label TEXT NOT NULL`
- `path TEXT`
- `url TEXT`
- `notes TEXT`
- `created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT local timestamp`

### `log`
- `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`
- `project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
- `ticket_id INTEGER REFERENCES tickets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
- `entry TEXT NOT NULL`
- `created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT local timestamp`

## State conventions

Project statuses seen in CLI:
- `active`
- `completed`
- `abandoned`
- `paused` (accepted by list filter)

Ticket statuses:
- `pending`
- `in-progress`
- `done`
- `skipped`

## Practical agent workflow examples

### Example 1: bootstrap
```bash
agentplan create "Website redesign" \
  --ticket "Audit current UX" \
  --ticket "Implement homepage" \
  --ticket "Add visual regression tests"
agentplan depend website-redesign 3 --on 2
```

### Example 2: execution loop
```bash
agentplan next website-redesign
agentplan ticket start website-redesign 2
# ... do work in repository ...
agentplan log website-redesign "Hero section migrated" --ticket 2
agentplan ticket done website-redesign 2
```

### Example 3: review and follow-up
```bash
agentplan status website-redesign --format compact
agentplan ticket add website-redesign "Fix mobile nav overflow" --depends 2
agentplan attach website-redesign "Preview" https://staging.example.com --ticket 4
```

## Notes for automation

- Project argument usually accepts slug or numeric id.
- Ticket arguments use per-project ticket number (`num`), not raw row id.
- For robust scripts, parse JSON mode from `status` when exact structure is needed.
